chapter.li: LEChapter1 Verse1 And now there was no more contention in all the land of Zarahemla, among all the people who belonged to king Benjamin, so that king Benjamin had continual peace all the remainder of his days. VerseEnd Verse2 And it came to pass that he had three sons, and he called their names Mosiah, and Helorum, and Helaman. And he caused that they should be taught in all the language of his fathers, that thereby they might become men of understanding, and that they might know concerning the prophecies which had been spoken by the mouths of their fathers, which were delivered them by the hand of the Lord. VerseEnd Verse3 And he also taught them concerning the records which were engraven upon the plates of brass, saying, My sons, I would that 2PP ye should remember that were it not for these plates which contain these records and these commandments, we must have suffered in ignorance, even at this present time, not knowing the mysteries of God. VerseEnd Verse4 For it were not possible that our father Lehi could have remembered all these things, to have taught them to his children, except it were for the help of these plates. For he having been taught in the language of the Egyptians, therefore he could read these engravings and teach them to his children, that thereby they could teach them to their children, and so fulfilling the commandments of God even down to this present time. VerseEnd Verse5 I say unto 2PP you my sons, were it not for these things which have been kept and preserved by the hand of God, that we might read and understand of his mysteries and have his commandments always before our eyes, that even our fathers would have dwindled in unbelief. And we should have been like unto our brethren the Lamanites, who know nothing concerning these things, or even do not believe them when they are taught them, because of the traditions of their fathers which are not correct. VerseEnd Verse6 O my sons, I would that 2PP ye should remember that these sayings are true, and also that these records are true. And behold also the plates of Nephi, which contain the records and the sayings of our fathers from the time they left Jerusalem until now; and they are true. And we can know of their surety because we have them before our eyes. VerseEnd Verse7 And now my sons, I would that 2PP ye should remember to search them diligently, that 2PP ye may profit thereby. And I would that 2PP ye should keep the commandments of God, that 2PP ye may prosper in the land according to the promises which the Lord made unto our fathers. VerseEnd Verse8 And many more things did king Benjamin teach his sons, which are not written in this book. VerseEnd

Verse9 And it came to pass that after king Benjamin had made an end of teaching his sons, that he waxed old and he saw that he must very soon go the way of all the earth. Therefore he thought it expedient that he should confer the kingdom upon one of his sons; VerseEnd Verse10 therefore he had Mosiah brought before him. And these are the words which he spake unto him, saying, My son, I would that 2PSF ye should make a proclamation throughout all this land, among all this people, or the people of Zarahemla and the people of Mosiah who dwell in this land, that thereby they may be gathered together; for on the morrow I shall proclaim unto this my people out of mine own mouth that 2PSI thou art a king and a ruler over this people whom the Lord our God hath given us. VerseEnd Verse11 And moreover, I shall give this people a name that thereby they may be distinguished above all the people which the Lord God hath brought out of the land of Jerusalem. And this I do because they have been a diligent people in keeping the commandments of the Lord. VerseEnd Verse12 And I give unto them a name that never shall be blotted out, except it be through transgression. VerseEnd Verse13 Yea, and moreover I say unto 2PSF you that if this highly favored people of the Lord should fall into transgression, and become a wicked and an adulterous people, that the Lord will deliver them up, that thereby they become weak like unto their brethren. And he will no more preserve them by his matchless and marvelous power as he has hitherto preserved our fathers. VerseEnd Verse14 For I say unto 2PSF you that if he had not extended his arm in the preservation of our fathers, they must have fallen into the hands of the Lamanites and become victims to their hatred. VerseEnd

Verse15 And it came to pass that after king Benjamin had made an end of these sayings to his son, that he gave him charge concerning all the affairs of the kingdom. VerseEnd Verse16 And moreover, he also gave him charge concerning the records which were engraven upon the plates of brass, and also the plates of Nephi, and also the sword of Laban, and the ball or director which led our fathers through the wilderness, which was prepared by the hand of the Lord that thereby they might be led, everyone, according to the heed and diligence which they gave unto him. VerseEnd Verse17 Therefore, as they were unfaithful, they did not prosper nor progress in their journey, but were driven back, and incurred the displeasure of God upon them. And therefore, they were smitten with famine and sore afflictions to stir them up in remembrance of their duty. VerseEnd

Verse18 And now it came to pass that Mosiah went and did as his father had commanded him, and proclaimed unto all the people who were in the land of Zarahemla, that thereby they might gather themselves together to go up to the temple to hear the words which his father should speak unto them. VerseEnd

LEChapter2 Verse1 And it came to pass that after Mosiah had done as his father had commanded him and had made a proclamation throughout all the land, that the people gathered themselves together throughout all the land, that they might go up to the temple to hear the words which king Benjamin should speak unto them. VerseEnd Verse2 And there were a great number, even so many that they did not number them, for they had multiplied exceedingly and waxed great in the land. VerseEnd Verse3 And they also took of the firstlings of their flocks, that they might offer sacrifice and burnt offerings according to the law of Moses, VerseEnd Verse4 and also that they might give thanks to the Lord their God, who had brought them out of the land of Jerusalem, and who had delivered them out of the hands of their enemies, and had appointed just men to be their teachers, and also a just man to be their king, who had established peace in the land of Zarahemla, and who had taught them to keep the commandments of God, that thereby they might rejoice and be filled with love towards God and all men. VerseEnd

Verse5 And it came to pass that when they came up to the temple, they pitched their tents round about, every man according to his family, consisting of his wife, and his sons, and his daughters, and their sons, and their daughters, from the eldest down to the youngest, every family being separate one from another. VerseEnd Verse6 And they pitched their tents round about the temple, every man having his tent with the door thereof towards the temple, that thereby they might remain in their tents and hear the words which king Benjamin should speak unto them. VerseEnd Verse7 For the multitude being so great that king Benjamin could not teach them all within the walls of the temple, therefore he caused a tower to be erected, that thereby his people might hear the words which he should speak unto them. VerseEnd

Verse8 And it came to pass that he began to speak to his people from the tower, and they could not all hear his words because of the greatness of the multitude. Therefore he caused that the words which he spake should be written and sent forth among those that were not under the sound of his voice, that they might also receive his words. VerseEnd Verse9 And these are the words which he spake and caused to be written, saying, My brethren, all 2PP ye that have assembled yourselves together, 2PP you that can hear my words which I shall speak unto 2PP you this day, for I have not commanded 2PP you to come up hither to trifle with the words which I shall speak, but that 2PP you should hearken unto me, and open 2PP your ears that 2PP ye may hear, and 2PP your hearts that 2PP ye may understand, and 2PP your minds that the mysteries of God may be unfolded to 2PP your view. VerseEnd Verse10 I have not commanded 2PP you to come up hither that 2PP ye should fear me, or that 2PP ye should think that I of myself am more than a mortal man. VerseEnd Verse11 But I am like as yourselves, subject to all manner of infirmities in body and mind. Yet as I have been chosen by this people, and was consecrated by my father, and was suffered by the hand of the Lord that I should be a ruler and a king over this people, and have been kept and preserved by his matchless power to serve 2PP thee with all the might, mind, and strength which the Lord hath granted unto me, VerseEnd Verse12 I say unto 2PP you that as I have been suffered to spend my days in 2PP your service, even up to this time, and have not sought gold, nor silver, nor any manner of riches of 2PP you, VerseEnd Verse13 neither have I suffered that 2PP ye should be confined in dungeons, nor that 2PP ye should make slaves one of another, or that 2PP ye should murder, or plunder, or steal, or commit adultery, or even I have not suffered that 2PP ye should commit any manner of wickedness, and have taught 2PP you that 2PP ye should keep the commandments of the Lord in all things which he hath commanded 2PP you. VerseEnd Verse14 And even I myself have labored with mine own hands that I might serve 2PP you, and that 2PP ye should not be laden with taxes, and that there should nothing come upon 2PP you which was grievous to be borne. And of all these things which I have spoken, 2PP ye yourselves are witnesses this day. VerseEnd Verse15 Yet my brethren, I have not done these things that I might boast, neither do I tell these things that thereby I might accuse 2PP you; but I tell 2PP you these things that 2PP ye may know that I can answer a clear conscience before God this day. VerseEnd Verse16 Behold, I say unto 2PP you that because I said unto 2PP you that I had spent my days in 2PP your service, I do not desire to boast, for I have only been in the service of God. VerseEnd

Verse17 And behold, I tell 2PP you these things that 2PP ye may learn wisdom, that 2PP ye may learn that when 2PP ye are in the service of 2PP your fellow beings, 2PP ye are only in the service of 2PP your God. VerseEnd Verse18 Behold, 2PP ye have called me 2PP your king. And if I, whom 2PP ye call 2PP your king, do labor to serve 2PP you, then had not 2PP ye ought to labor to serve one another? VerseEnd Verse19 And behold also, if I, whom 2PP ye call 2PP your king, who has spent his days in 2PP your service and yet has been in the service of God, doth merit any thanks from 2PP you, oh how had 2PP you ought to thank 2PP your Heavenly King! VerseEnd Verse20 I say unto 2PP you, my brethren, that if 2PP you should render all the thanks and praise which 2PP your whole souls have power to possess, to that God who has created 2PP you, and has kept and preserved 2PP you, and has caused that 2PP ye should rejoice, and has granted that 2PP ye should live in peace one with another — VerseEnd Verse21 I say unto 2PP you that if 2PP ye should serve him who has created 2PP you from the beginning, and art preserving 2PP you from day to day by lending 2PP you breath that 2PP ye may live, and move, and do according to 2PP your own will, and even supporting 2PP you from one moment to another — I say, if 2PP ye should serve him with all 2PP your whole soul, yet 2PP ye would be unprofitable servants. VerseEnd Verse22 And behold, all that he requires of 2PP you is to keep his commandments. And he has promised 2PP you that if 2PP ye would keep his commandments, 2PP ye should prosper in the land. And he never doth vary from that which he hath said. Therefore, if 2PP ye do keep his commandments, he doth bless 2PP you and prosper 2PP you. VerseEnd

Verse23 And now in the first place he hath created 2PP you, and granted unto 2PP you 2PP your lives, for which 2PP ye are indebted unto him. VerseEnd Verse24 And secondly, he doth require that 2PP ye should do as he has commanded 2PP you, for which, if 2PP ye do, he doth immediately bless 2PP you, and therefore he hath paid 2PP you. And 2PP ye are still indebted unto him, and are and will be for ever and ever. Therefore, of what have 2PP ye to boast? VerseEnd Verse25 And now I ask, can 2PP ye say aught of yourselves? I answer 2PP you, nay. 2PP Ye cannot say that 2PP thou art even as much as the dust of the earth, yet 2PP thou wast created of the dust of the earth; but behold, it belongeth to him who created 2PP you. VerseEnd Verse26 And I, even I, whom 2PP ye call 2PP your king, am no better than 2PP ye yourselves are, for I am also of the dust. And 2PP thou beholdest that I am old and am about to yield up this mortal frame to its mother earth. VerseEnd Verse27 Therefore, as I said unto 2PP you that I had served 2PP you, walking with a clear conscience before God, even so I at this time have caused that 2PP ye should assemble yourselves together, that I might be found blameless, and that 2PP your blood should not come upon me when I shall stand to be judged of God of the things whereof he hath commanded me concerning 2PP you. VerseEnd Verse28 I say unto 2PP you that I have caused that 2PP ye should assemble yourselves together that I might rid my garments of 2PP your blood at this period of time when I am about to go down to my grave, that I might go down in peace, and my immortal spirit may join the choirs above in singing the praises of a just God. VerseEnd Verse29 And moreover, I say unto 2PP you that I have caused that 2PP ye should assemble yourselves together that I might declare unto 2PP you that I can no longer be 2PP your teacher nor 2PP your king; VerseEnd Verse30 for even at this time my whole frame doth tremble exceedingly while attempting to speak unto 2PP you. But the Lord God doth support me, and hath suffered me that I should speak unto 2PP you, and hath commanded me that I should declare unto 2PP you this day that my son Mosiah is a king and a ruler over 2PP you. VerseEnd

Verse31 And now my brethren, I would that 2PP ye should do as 2PP ye have hitherto done. As 2PP ye have kept my commandments, and also the commandments of my father, and have prospered, and have been kept from falling into the hands of 2PP your enemies, even so, if 2PP ye shall keep the commandments of my son, or the commandments of God which shall be delivered unto 2PP you by him, 2PP ye shall prosper in the land and 2PP your enemies shall have no power over 2PP you. VerseEnd Verse32 But O my people, beware lest there shall arise contentions among 2PP you, and 2PP ye list to obey the evil spirit which was spoken of by my father, Mosiah. VerseEnd Verse33 For behold, there is a woe pronounced upon him who listeth to obey that spirit; for if he listeth to obey him, and remaineth and dieth in his sins, the same drinketh damnation to his own soul, for he receiveth for his wages an Everlasting punishment, having transgressed the law of God contrary to his own knowledge. VerseEnd Verse34 I say unto 2PP you that there are not any among 2PP you, except it be 2PP your little children, that have not been taught concerning these things but what knoweth that 2PP ye are eternally indebted to 2PP your Heavenly Father, to render to him all that 2PP you have and are, and also have been taught concerning the records which contain the prophecies which have been spoken by the holy prophets, even down to the time our father Lehi left Jerusalem, VerseEnd Verse35 and also all that has been spoken by our fathers until now. And behold also, they spake that which was commanded them of the Lord; therefore they are just and true. VerseEnd

Verse36 And now I say unto 2PP you, my brethren, that after 2PP ye have known and have been taught all these things, if 2PP ye should transgress and go contrary to that which has been spoken, that 2PP ye do withdraw yourselves from the spirit of the Lord, that it may have no place in 2PP you to guide 2PP you in wisdom’s paths that 2PP ye may be blessed, prospered, and preserved, VerseEnd Verse37 I say unto 2PP you that the man that doeth this, the same cometh out in open rebellion against God. Therefore, he listeth to obey the evil spirit and becometh an enemy to all righteousness. Therefore the Lord has no place in him, for he dwelleth not in unholy temples. VerseEnd Verse38 Therefore, if that man repenteth not, and remaineth and dieth an enemy to God, the demands of divine justice doth awaken his immortal soul to a lively sense of his own guilt, which doth cause him to shrink from the presence of the Lord, and doth fill his breast with guilt, and pain, and anguish, which is like an unquenchable fire whose flames ascendeth up for ever and ever. VerseEnd Verse39 And now I say unto 2PP you that mercy hath no claim on that man; therefore his final doom is to endure a never-ending torment. VerseEnd

Verse40 O all 2PP ye old men, and also 2PP ye young men, and 2PP you little children who can understand my words — for I have spoken plain unto 2PP you that 2PP ye might understand — I pray that 2PP ye should awake to a remembrance of the awful situation of those that have fallen into transgression. VerseEnd Verse41 And moreover, I would desire that 2PP ye should consider on the blessed and happy state of those that keep the commandments of God; for behold, they are blessed in all things, both temporal and spiritual. And if they hold out faithful to the end, they are received into Heaven, that thereby they may dwell with God in a state of never-ending happiness. O remember, remember that these things are true, for the Lord God hath spoken it. VerseEnd

LEChapter3 Verse1 And again my brethren, I would call 2PP your attention, for I have somewhat more to speak unto 2PP you. For behold, I have things to tell 2PP you concerning that which is to come. VerseEnd Verse2 And the things which I shall tell 2PP you are made known unto me by an angel from God. And he said unto me, Awake. And I awoke. And behold, he stood before me. VerseEnd Verse3 And he said unto me, Awake and hear the words which I shall tell 2PSI thee; for behold, I am come to declare unto 2PSI thee glad tidings of great joy. VerseEnd Verse4 For the Lord hath heard 2PSI thy prayers, and hath judged of 2PSI thy righteousness, and hath sent me to declare unto 2PSI thee that 2PSI thou mayest rejoice, and that 2PSI thou mayest declare unto 2PSI thy people that they may also be filled with joy. VerseEnd

Verse5 For behold, the time cometh and is not far distant that with power the Lord Omnipotent who reigneth, who was and is from all eternity to all eternity, shall come down from Heaven among the children of men, and shall dwell in a tabernacle of clay, and shall go forth amongst men, working mighty miracles such as healing the sick, raising the dead, causing the lame to walk, the blind to receive their sight, and the deaf to hear, and curing all manner of diseases. VerseEnd Verse6 And he shall cast out devils, or the evil spirits which dwell in the hearts of the children of men. VerseEnd Verse7 And lo, he shall suffer temptations and pain of body, hunger, thirst, and fatigue, even more than man can suffer except it be unto death. For behold, blood cometh from every pore, so great shall be his anguish for the wickedness and the abominations of his people. VerseEnd Verse8 And he shall be called Jesus Christ, the Son of God the Father of Heaven and of earth, the Creator of all things from the beginning; and his Mother shall be called Mary. VerseEnd Verse9 And lo, he cometh unto his own, that salvation might come unto the children of men, even through faith on his name. And even after all this, they shall consider him as a man and say that he hath a devil, and shall scourge him, and shall crucify him. VerseEnd Verse10 And he shall rise the third day from the dead.

And behold, he standeth to judge the world. And behold, all these things are done that a righteous judgment might come upon the children of men. VerseEnd Verse11 For behold, and also his blood atoneth for the sins of those who have fallen by the transgression of Adam, who have died not knowing the will of God concerning them, or who have ignorantly sinned. VerseEnd Verse12 But woe, woe unto him who knoweth that he rebelleth against God; for salvation cometh to none such except it be through repentance and faith on the Lord Jesus Christ. VerseEnd Verse13 And the Lord God hath sent his holy prophets among all the children of men to declare these things to every kindred, nation, and tongue, that thereby whosoever should believe that Christ should come, the same might receive remission of their sins and rejoice with exceeding great joy, even as though he had already come among them. VerseEnd

Verse14 Yet the Lord God saw that his people were a stiffnecked people, and he appointed unto them a law, even the law of Moses. VerseEnd Verse15 And many signs, and wonders, and types, and shadows shewed he unto them concerning his coming; and also holy prophets spake unto them concerning his coming. And yet they hardened their hearts and understood not that the law of Moses availeth nothing except it were through the atonement of his blood. VerseEnd Verse16 And even if it were possible that little children could sin, they could not be saved. But I say unto 2PP you, they are blessed; for behold, as in Adam or by nature they fall, even so the blood of Christ atoneth for their sins. VerseEnd Verse17 And moreover, I say unto 2PP you that there shall be no other name given, nor any other way nor means, whereby salvation can come unto the children of men, only in and through the name of Christ the Lord Omnipotent. VerseEnd Verse18 For behold, he judgeth, and his judgment is just. And the infant perisheth not that dieth in his infancy, but men drink damnation to their own souls except they humble themselves, and become as little children, and believe that salvation was, and is, and is to come, in and through the atoning blood of Christ, the Lord Omnipotent. VerseEnd Verse19 For the natural man is an enemy to God, and has been from the fall of Adam, and will be for ever and ever but if he yields to the enticings of the holy spirit, and putteth off the natural man, and becometh a saint through the atonement of Christ the Lord, and becometh as a child: submissive, meek, humble, patient, full of love, willing to submit to all things which the Lord seeth fit to inflict upon him, even as a child doth submit to his father. VerseEnd

Verse20 And moreover, I say unto 2PP you that the time shall come when the knowledge of a savior shall spread throughout every nation, kindred, tongue, and people. VerseEnd Verse21 And behold, when that time cometh, none shall be found blameless before God, except it be little children, only through repentance and faith on the name of the Lord God Omnipotent. VerseEnd Verse22 And even at this time, when 2PSI thou shalt have taught 2PSI thy people the things which the Lord 2PSI thy God hath commanded 2PSI thee, even then are they found no more blameless in the sight of God, only according to the words which I have spoken unto 2PSI thee. VerseEnd

Verse23 And now I have spoken the words which the Lord God hath commanded me. VerseEnd Verse24 And thus saith the Lord: They shall stand as a bright testimony against this people at the judgment day, whereof they shall be judged, every man according to his works, whether they be good or whether they be evil. VerseEnd Verse25 And if they be evil, they are consigned to an awful view of their own guilt and abominations, which doth cause them to shrink from the presence of the Lord into a state of misery and Endless torment, from whence they can no more return. Therefore, they have drunk damnation to their own souls. VerseEnd Verse26 Therefore, they have drunk out of the cup of the wrath of God, which justice could no more deny unto them than it could deny that Adam should fall because of his partaking of the forbidden fruit. Therefore, mercy could have claim on them no more for ever, VerseEnd Verse27 and their torment is as a lake of fire and brimstone whose flames are unquenchable and whose smoke ascendeth up for ever and ever. Thus hath the Lord commanded me. Amen. VerseEnd
